claim: HIPV-emitting N. attenuata plants produced twice as many buds and flowers as HIPV-silenced plants when native Geocoris spp. predators reduced herbivore loads by 50% on HIPV-emitters.
source_text: HIPV-emitting N. attenuata plants produced twice as many buds and flowers as HIPV-silenced plants, but only when native Geocoris spp. predators reduced herbivore loads (by 50%) on HIPV-emitters.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data from the 2-year field study described in the manuscript, specifically the results shown in Figures 6 and 9.

claim: TPI-producing plants were not fitter than TPI-silenced plants.
source_text: TPI-producing plants were not fitter than TPI-silenced plants.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data comparing reproductive output between TPI-producing and TPI-silenced plants in the field study.

claim: TPIs weaken a specialist herbivore's behavioral evasive responses to simulated Geocoris spp. attack.
source_text: TPIs weakened a specialist herbivore's behavioral evasive responses to simulated Geocoris spp. attack
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data from mock predation assays shown in Figure 10 and Videos 1-4.

claim: TPIs function against specialists by enhancing indirect defense.
source_text: TPIs function against specialists by enhancing indirect defense.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is inferred from the data showing TPIs weaken herbivore evasive responses, combined with the observation that this could enhance predation effectiveness.

claim: Plant indirect defenses are traits that disable or remove herbivores by manipulating tri-trophic interactions to the advantage of the plant.
source_text: Plant indirect defenses are traits that disable or remove herbivores by manipulating tri-trophic interactions to the advantage of the plant
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citation to Price et al., 1980 and represents established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: HIPVs can reduce herbivore loads by 24% to more than 90% by increasing both predation and parasitization of herbivores.
source_text: Field studies with the native tobacco Nicotiana attenuata, a desert annual, and with maize have shown that HIPVs can reduce herbivore loads by 24% to more than 90%, by increasing both predation and parasitization of herbivores
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by multiple citations to previous field studies (Kessler and Baldwin, 2001; Rasmann et al., 2005; Halitschke et al., 2008; Degenhardt et al., 2009; Allmann and Baldwin, 2010).

claim: It remains unclear whether HIPVs increase plant fitness in nature.
source_text: it is not clear whether HIPVs increase plant fitness in nature
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on a review of existing literature and the observation that previous studies have not demonstrated fitness benefits.

claim: Previous field studies on HIPVs have either spanned too short a time to reveal Darwinian fitness benefits, or have not reported fitness data at all.
source_text: The field studies described above have either spanned too short a time to reveal Darwinian fitness benefits, or have not reported fitness data at all
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on a review of cited field studies (Kessler and Baldwin, 2001; Rasmann et al., 2005; Halitschke et al., 2008; Degenhardt et al., 2009; Allmann and Baldwin, 2010).

claim: Three decades after their description, it remains unclear whether HIPVs are really indirect defenses.
source_text: Hence three decades after their description, it remains unclear whether HIPVs are really indirect defenses.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on a review of the literature and the gap in evidence for fitness benefits of HIPVs.

claim: Long-term field studies comparing HIPV-emitting vs -deficient plants are required to demonstrate a defensive function for HIPVs.
source_text: Long-term field studies comparing HIPV-emitting vs -deficient plants are required in order to demonstrate a defensive function for HIPVs.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is inferred from the identified gap in previous research and the requirements for demonstrating fitness benefits.

claim: The inducibility of HIPV emission is likely essential for HIPV function because it ensures association with herbivore feeding.
source_text: Thus the inducibility of HIPV emission, which ensures association with herbivore feeding, is likely essential for HIPV function
evidence_reasoning: This claim is inferred from cited evidence that naïve predators and parasitoids learn to associate HIPVs with prey (Allison and Hare, 2009).

claim: Genetically silencing the biosynthesis of HIPVs permits naturally inducible wild-type plants to serve as HIPV emitters for comparison with transformed lines lacking specific volatile components.
source_text: Genetically silencing the biosynthesis of HIPVs, however, permits naturally inducible wild-type (WT) plants to serve as HIPV emitters, for comparison with transformed lines lacking specific volatile components
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to previous work (Halitschke et al., 2008; Skibbe et al., 2008) and represents an established methodological approach.

claim: Plant direct defenses can slow herbivore growth and prolong vulnerability to predators and parasitoids as postulated by the slow growth-high mortality hypothesis.
source_text: Many herbivores can outgrow their vulnerability to predators and parasitoids, but plant direct defenses can slow herbivore growth and prolong vulnerability as postulated by the slow growth-high mortality hypothesis
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by multiple citations (Benrey and Denno, 1997; Williams, 1999; Kessler and Baldwin, 2001, 2004; Kaplan and Thaler, 2011).

claim: Manduca sexta and M. quinquemaculata are resistant to the potent alkaloid toxin nicotine.
source_text: The solanaceous specialists Manduca sexta and M. quinquemaculata (Lepidoptera, Sphingidae) are resistant to the potent alkaloid toxin nicotine
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citation to Wink and Theile, 2002.

claim: Manduca sexta and M. quinquemaculata are sensitive to the nutritional value of plant tissue.
source_text: The solanaceous specialists Manduca sexta and M. quinquemaculata (Lepidoptera, Sphingidae) are...sensitive to the nutritional value of plant tissue
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citation to Zavala and Baldwin, 2004.

claim: Trypsin protease inhibitors slow the growth of M. sexta on N. attenuata.
source_text: trypsin protease inhibitors (TPIs) slow the growth of M. sexta on N. attenuata
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citation to Zavala et al., 2008.

claim: TPI-producing N. attenuata plants produce more seeds than TPI-deficient plants when attacked by M. sexta under controlled glasshouse conditions.
source_text: Although TPI-producing N. attenuata plants produce more seeds than TPI-deficient plants when attacked by M. sexta under controlled glasshouse conditions
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citation to Zavala and Baldwin, 2004.

claim: Whether TPIs function as a direct defense in nature is unknown.
source_text: whether TPIs function as a direct defense in nature is unknown.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is inferred from the gap between glasshouse studies and field studies.

claim: N. attenuata is an annual, opportunistic out-crosser that produces seeds within one growing season, mostly from fertilization via self-pollen.
source_text: Because N. attenuata is an annual, opportunistic out-crosser, seeds are produced within one growing season, mostly from fertilization via self-pollen
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citation to Sime and Baldwin, 2003.

claim: Bud and flower production can be related to lifetime seed production in N. attenuata, which is commonly accepted as a measure of Darwinian fitness.
source_text: we can relate bud and flower production to lifetime seed production, which is commonly accepted as a measure of Darwinian fitness
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations (Baldwin, 1998; van Loon et al., 2000; Hoballah and Turlings, 2001) and represents accepted practice in plant fitness studies.

claim: Manduca spp. larvae cause the most defoliation of N. attenuata plants in the Great Basin Desert of southwestern Utah in many years.
source_text: In many years, Manduca spp. larvae cause the most defoliation of N. attenuata plants in this area
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citation to Kessler and Baldwin, 2001.

claim: Eggs and young larvae of Manduca spp. are predated by Geocoris spp. which occur naturally in the Utah habitat.
source_text: Eggs and young larvae of Manduca spp. are predated by Geocoris spp. (big-eyed bugs) which occur naturally in the Utah habitat
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to Kessler and Baldwin, 2001; Halitschke et al., 2008; Skibbe et al., 2008.

claim: Utah Geocoris spp. predators are attracted to the sesquiterpene (E)-α-bergamotene as well as green leaf volatiles.
source_text: Specifically, Utah Geocoris spp. predators are attracted to the sesquiterpene (E)-α-bergamotene as well as green leaf volatiles (fatty acid-derived C6 aldehydes, alcohols and esters)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to Kessler and Baldwin, 2001; Halitschke et al., 2008; Schuman et al., 2009.

claim: Green leaf volatiles can be silenced via a single upstream 13-lipoxygenase, NaLOX2, which specifically supplies lipid hydroperoxides for their production.
source_text: Green leaf volatiles, or GLVs, can be silenced via a single upstream 13-lipoxygenase, NaLOX2, which specifically supplies lipid hydroperoxides for their production
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citation to Allmann et al., 2010.

claim: The oral secretions of M. sexta convert 3-(Z)-GLVs to the 2-(E)-structures, resulting in greater Geocoris spp. predation than the damage-induced (Z):(E) ratio.
source_text: the oral secretions (OS) of M. sexta convert 3-(Z)-GLVs to the 2-(E)-structures, resulting in greater Geocoris spp. predation than the damage-induced (Z):(E) ratio
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citation to Allmann and Baldwin, 2010.

claim: GLVs are released immediately upon damage.
source_text: GLVs are released immediately upon damage
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citation to Allmann and Baldwin, 2010.

claim: GLVs prime or directly regulate responses in neighboring plants.
source_text: GLVs prime or directly regulate responses in neighboring plants
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to Kessler et al., 2006; Paschold et al., 2006.

claim: GLVs attract herbivores as well as predators.
source_text: GLVs...attract herbivores as well as predators
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citation to Halitschke et al., 2008.

claim: GLVs are important cues for pollinating and ovipositing moths.
source_text: GLVs...are important cues for pollinating and ovipositing moths
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to Kessler and Baldwin, 2001, 2006; De Moraes et al., 2001; Fraser et al., 2003.

claim: GLVs stimulate Manduca spp. feeding.
source_text: GLVs also stimulate Manduca spp. feeding
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to Halitschke et al., 2004; Meldau et al., 2009.

claim: Silencing plant GLV production results in reduced herbivore damage.
source_text: silencing plant GLV production results in reduced herbivore damage
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to Halitschke et al., 2004; Meldau et al., 2009.

claim: The irPI plants had no detectable TPI activity in the glasshouse or throughout the field experiment in 2011.
source_text: The irPI plants (Steppuhn and Baldwin, 2007) had no detectable TPI activity in the glasshouse or throughout the field experiment in 2011
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental measurements shown in Figure 1.

claim: PI transcripts accumulated to only 0.3% of WT levels in irPI.
source_text: PI transcripts accumulated to only 0.3% of WT levels in irPI
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data from qPCR measurements shown in Figure 1B.

claim: TPI activity and PI transcripts were similar to WT plants in irLOX2 and hemi-irLOX2.
source_text: TPI activity and PI transcripts were similar to WT plants in irLOX2 and hemi-irLOX2
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental measurements shown in Figure 1.

claim: GLVs in hemi-irLOX2 plants were reduced to 20-40% of WT levels.
source_text: GLVs in hemi-irLOX2 plants were reduced to 20-40% of WT levels
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental measurements of GLV pools and emissions shown in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: GLVs in irLOX2 plants were reduced to less than 10% of WT levels.
source_text: GLVs in...irLOX2 plants were reduced to less than 10% of WT levels
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental measurements of GLV pools and emissions shown in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: The emission of (E)-α-bergamotene does not differ significantly among the lines used.
source_text: the emission of (E)-α-bergamotene, the best-characterized HIPV in N. attenuata apart from GLVs...does not differ significantly among the lines used
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental measurements of (E)-α-bergamotene emission from glasshouse-grown plants.

claim: The transformation process itself does not affect plant fitness or competitive ability.
source_text: The transformation process itself does not affect plant fitness or competitive ability
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citation to Schwachtje et al., 2008.

claim: Geocoris spp. predated 35-37% of larvae from GLV-supplemented plants vs 22-27% from control plants in the first trial of M2.
source_text: Geocoris spp. tended to predate more larvae from GLV-supplemented plants (Fisher's exact tests, 35–37% vs 22–27% May 5–6, p=0.066
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data from predation assays shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Geocoris spp. predated 17-21% of larvae from GLV-supplemented plants vs 12% from control plants in the second trial of M2.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data from predation assays shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Predation of larvae without GLV supplementation was 43%/60% (WT/irPI) vs 17%/33% (irLOX2/hemi-irLOX2) during M3.
source_text: Predation of both larvae and eggs without GLV supplementation was two to four times as great on GLV-emitting WT and irPI plants: 43%/60% (WT/irPI) for larvae...vs 17%/33% (irLOX2/hemi-irLOX2) for larvae
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data from predation assays shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Predation of eggs without GLV supplementation was 34%/39% (WT/irPI) vs 9%/20% (irLOX2/hemi-irLOX2) during M3.
source_text: 34%/39% for eggs, vs...9%/20% for eggs
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data from predation assays shown in Figure 5C.

claim: There was no difference among plant genotypes in the number of Geocoris spp. individuals surveying plants.
source_text: However, there was no difference among plant genotypes in the number of Geocoris spp. individuals (p>0.05 in Fisher's exact tests), indicating that Geocoris spp. regularly survey all plants and use GLVs as a short-distance cue to determine which plants harbor prey.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by Geocoris spp. count data in Table 2, and the inference about GLV use is based on this observation combined with predation data.

claim: M. sexta feeding significantly affected growth and reproduction of plants overall in 2011.
source_text: Although M. sexta feeding significantly affected growth and reproduction of plants overall
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of growth and reproduction data shown in Figure 6 and Table 3.

claim: The effect of M. sexta feeding was not significant for irLOX2 or irPI plants in either year.
source_text: the effect was not significant for irLOX2 or irPI plants in either year
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by statistical analysis of growth and reproduction data shown in Figure 6 and Table 3.

claim: irLOX2 plants suffered 60% less mirid and noctuid damage by the end of M3 in 2011.
source_text: irLOX2 plants suffered 60% less mirid and noctuid damage by the end of M3 in 2011
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by herbivore damage assessment data shown in Figure 7B.

claim: In 2010, in the absence of Geocoris spp. predation, genotypes did not differ in M. sexta mortality or plant reproduction.
source_text: In the absence of Geocoris spp. in 2010, genotypes did not differ in M. sexta mortality (N=51 larvae)—which in every observed case was due to a failure of the larva to feed—or plant reproduction (N=17 plants)
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data from the 2010 field season shown in Figure 9A.

claim: Larval mortality on hemi-irLOX2 was only half as great as on WT or irPI when larvae transitioned from the second to third instar in 2011.
source_text: Larval mortality (upper panel) reached a maximum of 76% after larvae transitioned from the second to third instar (days 9 and 10), at which time larval mortality on hemi-irLOX2 was only half as great as on WT or irPI
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data from the 2011 M4 infestation shown in Figure 9B.

claim: By the end of the M4 assay, hemi-irLOX2 plants had produced 40-50% fewer buds and flowers than matched WT and irPI plants.
source_text: By the end of the assay, the hemi-irLOX2 plants had produced 40–50% fewer buds and flowers than matched WT and irPI plants
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data from the 2011 M4 infestation shown in Figure 9B.

claim: Unripe seed capsules on hemi-irLOX2 plants were reduced by 50% compared to WT and irPI.
source_text: This reduced bud and flower production was not due to accelerated seed set: unripe seed capsules on hemi-irLOX2 plants were also reduced by 50%
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data from the 2011 M4 infestation shown in Figure 9B.

claim: Herbivore-induced GLV emissions function as indirect defenses by increasing predation of Manduca spp. twofold, resulting in a twofold increase in bud and flower production for N. attenuata in its native habitat.
source_text: These data demonstrate that herbivore-induced GLV emissions function as indirect defenses by increasing predation of Manduca spp. larvae twofold, resulting in a twofold increase in bud and flower production for N. attenuata in its native habitat.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is inferred from the combined data on predation rates and plant reproduction from the field experiments, particularly the M4 infestation in 2011.

claim: M. sexta and M. quinquemaculata did not differ in their growth or instar progression on plants.
source_text: M. sexta and M. quinquemaculata did not differ in their growth or instar progression
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data analyzing larval growth by species during the M4 infestation.

claim: Wild Manduca spp. larvae fed on WT leaves were 50% less likely to successfully attack a toothpick in simulated predator attacks compared to larvae fed on irPI leaves.
source_text: larvae fed on WT leaves were 50% less likely to successfully attack the toothpick
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data from on-plant mock predation assays shown in Figure 10A.

claim: Laboratory M. sexta larvae fed on WT leaves were 50% less likely to successfully attack an insect pin in simulated predator attacks compared to larvae fed on irPI leaves.
source_text: Similarly to the on-plant assay, larvae fed on WT leaves were 50% less likely to successfully attack the insect pin, either when initially poked, or poked and lifted with the pin
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data from off-plant mock predation assays shown in Figure 10B.

claim: WT-fed larvae ceased to grow for at least 24 hr after simulated attack, while irPI-fed larvae continued to grow.
source_text: We also monitored recovery post-trial and found that WT-fed larvae ceased to grow for at least 24 hr after simulated attack, while irPI-fed larvae continued to grow
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by experimental data from off-plant mock predation assays shown in Figure 10B.

claim: TPIs may support indirect defense by weakening the response of larvae to predator attack.
source_text: Thus TPIs did not increase plant reproduction under attack from Manduca spp. in nature, but may support indirect defense by weakening the response of larvae to predator attack.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing reduced evasive responses in TPI-fed larvae combined with the lack of direct fitness benefits from TPIs.

claim: The irPI construct was not active in the hemizygous state in hemi-irLOX2 plants.
source_text: The hemi-irLOX2 plants used in this study were created by crossing homozygous irPI and irLOX2 plants, but the irPI construct was not active in the hemizygous state
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by TPI activity and transcript measurements shown in Figure 1.

claim: Functional RNAi constructs may be rendered ineffective as a result of insufficient gene dosage when present in the hemizygous state.
source_text: It is common molecular biology knowledge that functional RNAi constructs may be rendered ineffective as a result of insufficient gene dosage...which may occur when an RNAi construct is present in the hemizygous state
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citation to Travella et al., 2006 and references therein, and represents established knowledge in molecular biology.

claim: Fewer than 5% of buds and flowers are aborted by healthy field-grown N. attenuata plants.
source_text: For field-grown N. attenuata plants, fewer than 5% of buds and flowers (in total) are aborted by healthy (not diseased) plants
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on observational data from field experiments (M C Schuman and I T Baldwin, personal observation, June 2010).

claim: More than 70% of seed set from plants in native N. attenuata populations results from fertilization via self-pollen.
source_text: Plants are self-compatible and more than 70% of seed set from plants in native populations results from fertilization via self-pollen
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citation to Sime and Baldwin, 2003.

claim: Numbers of buds and flowers correlate to lifetime seed capsule production in N. attenuata.
source_text: Thus numbers of buds and flowers correlate to lifetime seed capsule production
evidence_reasoning: This claim is inferred from the low abortion rate and self-compatibility of N. attenuata.

claim: Lifetime seed capsule production correlates to lifetime seed production in N. attenuata.
source_text: Thus numbers of buds and flowers correlate to lifetime seed capsule production, which in turn correlates to lifetime seed production
evidence_reasoning: This claim is logically inferred from the relationship between seed capsules and seed production.

claim: Lifetime seed production has been used as a proxy measure of Darwinian fitness in N. attenuata.
source_text: which in turn correlates to lifetime seed production, which has been used as a proxy measure of Darwinian fitness
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to Baldwin, 1998; van Loon et al., 2000; Hoballah and Turlings, 2001.

claim: The transgenic lines used do not vary in seed mass or their seedling viability under laboratory conditions.
source_text: The transgenic lines used do not vary in seed mass or their seedling viability under laboratory conditions.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on unstated experimental observations of the transgenic lines.

claim: HIPVs can be employed as part of integrated pest management strategies which rely on recruiting biological control agents to reduce pesticide use.
source_text: By indicating the long-sought indirect defensive function of HIPVs, these data set the stage for the use of HIPVs as part of integrated pest management strategies (IPM), which rely in part on recruiting biological control agents to reduce pesticide use
evidence_reasoning: This claim is inferred from the demonstrated defensive function of HIPVs combined with cited knowledge about IPM strategies (Horne and Page, 2008).

claim: IPM biological control agents are usually naturally occurring generalist parasitoids and predators, such as Geocoris spp.
source_text: These agents are usually naturally occurring generalist parasitoids and predators, such as Geocoris spp.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to Eubanks and Denno, 1999, 2000; Allison and Hare, 2009; Allmann and Baldwin, 2010.

claim: IPM would benefit from selective breeding or engineering of HIPV emission rather than relying on controlled release dispensers.
source_text: IPM would benefit from selective breeding or engineering of HIPV emission (Kos et al., 2009) rather than relying on alternatives such as controlled release dispensers, which have mixed success and require large amounts of synthetic HIPVs
evidence_reasoning: This claim is inferred from the demonstrated effectiveness of endogenous HIPV production combined with cited limitations of alternative approaches (Kos et al., 2009; Kaplan, 2012).

claim: PIs may be employed to enhance the efficiency of indirect defense, especially combined with toxins like Bt.
source_text: PIs may be employed to enhance the efficiency of indirect defense, especially combined with toxins like Bt that directly target herbivores and are safe for biological control agents.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is speculative, based on the observed effects of PIs on herbivore behavior in response to predation.

claim: Indirect defenses promise an effective 'first line of defense' against agricultural pests, to which not even specialist herbivores are likely to rapidly evolve resistance.
source_text: indirect defenses promise an effective 'first line of defense' against agricultural pests, to which not even specialist herbivores are likely to rapidly evolve resistance.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is speculative, inferred from the demonstrated effectiveness of indirect defenses and concerns about Bt resistance.

claim: The induction of all HIPVs except GLVs is mediated by jasmonate signaling in the 'UT' genotype of N. attenuata.
source_text: For the 'UT' genotype of N. attenuata used in our experiments, the induction of all HIPVs except GLVs is mediated by jasmonate signaling
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to Halitschke and Baldwin, 2003; Kessler et al., 2004.

claim: The irPI line A-04-186-1 and irLOX2 line A-04-52-2 are not affected in jasmonate signaling.
source_text: The irPI line A-04-186-1 (Steppuhn and Baldwin, 2007) and irLOX2 line A-04-52-2 (Allmann et al., 2010) have been characterized previously, and neither is affected in jasmonate signaling.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to previous characterizations of these lines (Steppuhn and Baldwin, 2007; Allmann et al., 2010).

claim: Both G. pallens and G. punctipes were present in the field site in 2011, but most individuals observed on and around plants were G. pallens.
source_text: both G. pallens and G. punctipes were present in 2011, but most individuals observed on and around plants were G. pallens.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is based on observational data from field monitoring of Geocoris spp. populations.

claim: Larvae beyond the third instar are not susceptible to Geocoris spp. predation.
source_text: larvae beyond this stage are not susceptible to Geocoris spp.
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citation to Kessler and Baldwin, 2001.

claim: M. sexta and M. quinquemaculata oral secretions are highly similar in their composition.
source_text: M. sexta and M. quinquemaculata oral secretions (OS) are highly similar in their composition
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citation to Halitschke et al., 2001.

claim: M. sexta and M. quinquemaculata oral secretions elicit similar volatiles in N. attenuata.
source_text: M. sexta and M. quinquemaculata oral secretions (OS)...elicit similar volatiles...in N. attenuata
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citations to Halitschke et al., 2001; Kessler and Baldwin, 2001.

claim: M. sexta and M. quinquemaculata oral secretions elicit similar defense genes in N. attenuata.
source_text: M. sexta and M. quinquemaculata oral secretions (OS)...elicit similar...defense genes in N. attenuata
evidence_reasoning: This claim is supported by citation to Schittko et al., 2001.
